title: Germany news: Berlin hosts digital summit with AI focus
summary: A government-run conference is to look at the uses and dangers of artificial intelligence. This comes as the German and UK defense ministers will discuss expanding AI's role in military cooperation.…

blocks.text: A government-run conference is to look at the uses and dangers of artificial intelligence. This comes as the German and UK defense ministers will discuss expanding AI's role in military cooperation. DW has more.

blocks.caption: Chancellor Merz is to have an encounter of the robotic kind at the digital summit (FILE: 22.10)Image: Marco Einfeldt/SZ Photo/picture alliance

items: The Digital Summit in Berlin is to focus on how best to bring Germany and Europe up to speed in the field of artificial intelligence (AI)
Chancellor Merz is scheduled to speak to guests — and be introduced to a humanoid robot
Separately, the German and UK defense ministers are to discuss incorporating AI more into military cooperation between their two countries
A 34-year-old man is to go on trial in Leipzig accused of carrying out a deadly hit-and-run accident six months ago in which two people were killed
German gas storage levels are well below those prescribed by law ahead of the heating season

blocks.text: This is a round-up of some of the top headlines from and about Germany on November 2, 2026:
Government to open AI-focused Digital Summit in Berlin

blocks.caption: Could this soon be a common sight in German households?Image: NEURA Robotics

blocks.text: A two-day conference in Berlin that will look at ways of enhancing Germany's digital infrastructure, particularly in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), is to be opened by the minister for digital affairs, Karsten Wildberger, on Monday morning.

More than 1,000 guests, including digital ministers from Europe and Canada, are expected to attend the summit, which this year will focus largely on the uses and safety of AI and new developments in the field.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz is scheduled to hold a speech in the afternoon and to meet with a robot from the German company Neura Robotics.
The company develops robots that can see, hear and feel and are potentially utilizable in both industries and households.
The event is being held for the 19th time since its inception in 2006 as the National IT Summit. It did not take place in 2021, an election year in Germany.
